**Abstract**

Solar and wind energy is growing fast and can contribute significantly to meet the goals set by many countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Although the benefits of solar and wind energy are obvious and great, negative perception of these technologies can inhibit their wide penetration in some regions.

INTRODUCTION

However, every energy conversion and transmission activity affects the environment. The use of fossil fuels can pollute land, air and water and can impact wildlife and the landscape.

Solar energy

Solar energy installations can be distributed or large scale depends on the size and location. Large scale solar installations are geographically centralized and sometimes built far away from where the power is needed, e.g. in deserts where the solar irradiation is high and the population density is low [ [7](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)].

Solar energy is a great alternative to carbon-intensive energy sources and has enormous potential to minimize polluting emissions and thus contribute to climate change mitigation [ [8](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)]. Zhai _et al._ [ [9](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] found that the total amount of avoided CO2 emissions can range from 6.5% to 18.8% if 10% of the power in 10 different states in the US were generated from PV.

Solar PV power generation plays a significant and growing role in many countries. In developing countries, off-grid solar PV systems continue to contribute to the electrification of rural areas. It is believed that 5% of the people in Africa are powered by off-grid PV systems [ [10](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)].

Figure 1

The global installed PV and CSP capacity (GW)

![](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/getXMLobject.php?objData=bzB6c3JnWGpQWjQ1NnJ1ZDFMQlcxZz09,image1.png)

Despite the advantages of solar energy, it hurts the environment.

Wind Energy

In the year 2018, the global wind power market grew by 51 GW to reach the total installed capacity of 591 GW ( [Figure 2](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)) [ [10](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)]. Most of the wind turbines in the world (96%) are onshore wind turbines.

The power capacity and size of modern wind turbines are becoming larger with time. Large wind turbines have a larger swept area, they are powerful, and can reduce the cost of the generated renewable power.

Figure 2

The global wind energy (installed GW)

![](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/getXMLobject.php?objData=bzB6c3JnWGpQWjQ1NnJ1ZDFMQlcxZz09,image2.png)

Figure 3

Wind and solar energies - the top six countries

![](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/getXMLobject.php?objData=bzB6c3JnWGpQWjQ1NnJ1ZDFMQlcxZz09,image3.png)

Despite that wind power is environmentally benign, it still has some impact on human life [ [26](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)]. For example, Raadal _et al._ [ [27](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] [ [28](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] showed that onshore wind turbines with a capacity between 30 kW and 3MW can generate total emissions of 4.6–55.6g CO2 /kWh. In another study conducted by Lenzen and Munksgaard [ [29](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)], higher values of greenhouse gas emissions (7.9 to 123.7g CO2 /kWh) are reported for onshore wind turbines with a capacity between 0.3 kW and 3 MW.

Solar and wind systems are raising in various regions in the world and are no longer specific anymore to coastal, mountainous, desert or arid regions. This impact on the environment varies according to the system type and its geographical location on the planet.

Both wind and solar systems have shown significant growth in the last years, they also have a significant impact on the environment, such as noise, biodiversity impact, visual and climatic impact. Although the above-mentioned impacts seem insignificant when compared with traditional fuels, their impact on the whole ecosystem shouldn’t be ignored. It is important to investigate these negative impacts, especially the potential of long-term impact in order to come up with intelligent solutions to maintain the sustainability of solar and wind energy.

ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF SOLAR ENERGY

Both concentrated solar thermal and photovoltaic solar plants have an impact on the environment. This impact varies depending on the size and type of the solar plants.

Impact on biodiversity

The integration of small-scale distributed installations or large scale solar plants into the built environment will likely have a negligible direct impact on biodiversity [ [31](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)]. In this section, the impact of both CSP and PV plants on undisturbed habitats will be the focus of the discussion.

The graded soil and new roads can further increase organisms' mortality rates and the extinction of native species [ [36](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] [ [37](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)].

In arid or semiarid regions, the desert vegetation controls the transport of sand, dust, and sediments. Removal of vegetation, grading the land and the construction of roads by solar energy infrastructure causes soil loss by storms and floods [ [38](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] [ [39](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)].

Large scale solar energy infrastructures may block the movement as well as seasonal migration of wildlife species which may cause a gene migration disruption between different species [ [40](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)] [ [41](https://www.sdewes.org/jsdewes/pid9.0387#)]. # Why wind and solar are key solutions to combat climate change
### We know the world needs deep and rapid cuts in CO2 emissions to keep us on track for 1.5 degrees. The deepest cuts this decade need to happen in the world’s highest-emitting sector – the power sector. This is because decarbonising the power sector is relatively cheap and straightforward, and because doing so opens the door to a global economy running almost entirely on clean energy.
Wind and solar are the cheapest, the quickest to deploy and among the cleanest, least carbon-intensive power sources.

# Hello there!
## Why not click on a circle?
### Wind and solar are the cheapest solutions
Solar and wind power costs have been declining rapidly. [During the decade to 2020](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg3/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGIII_SummaryForPolicymakers.pdf), the cost of wind and solar power fell by 55% and 85%, respectively. The cost of batteries, increasingly used to store renewable electricity, also fell by 85% over the same time period.

Overall, wind and solar costs [have continued to fall](https://about.bnef.com/blog/2h-2023-lcoe-update-an-uneven-recovery/) since 2020 despite supply chain issues relating to the Covid-19 pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, which produced a short-term uptick in wind power costs in some regions. Analysts foresee continuing cost reductions for both wind and solar in the coming years.

LCOE Global Totals

When considered over an asset’s lifetime, the cost of producing a unit of electricity from onshore wind and solar PV, is now generally [well below that of gas and coal](https://about.bnef.com/blog/2h-2023-lcoe-update-an-uneven-recovery/) in many countries. In some cases it is even cheaper to build and run new wind or solar farms than to continue running existing fossil fuel plants.

This is more than 0.5% of global GDP. Globally, [the quicker the transition, the greater the savings](https://www.cell.com/joule/pdf/S2542-4351(22)00410-X.pdf).

### Wind and solar are quick to deploy
The amount of wind and solar capacity added every year is far [outpacing growth](https://www.irena.org/News/pressreleases/2023/Mar/Record-9-point-6-Percentage-Growth-in-Renewables-Achieved-Despite-Energy-Crisis) in both fossil fuel capacity and alternative clean technologies. Solar’s capacity growth in particular has regularly [exceeded forecasts](https://twitter.com/AukeHoekstra/status/1507047932226375688?lang=en).

RES cumulative capacity additions IRENA

Meanwhile, other clean technologies such as nuclear power plants and large hydro dams can take multiple years to build, a major reason why  wind and solar will be crucial in [providing the majority of new clean generation this decade](https://www.iea.org/reports/net-zero-roadmap-a-global-pathway-to-keep-the-15-0c-goal-in-reach) – as much as 89%, according to International Energy Agency (IEA) Net Zero pathways.

They can be built anywhere, and tend to face few restrictions due to security or public [safety concerns](https://yougov.co.uk/international/articles/39858-what-do-europeans-and-americans-think-about-nuclea?redirect_from=%2Ftopics%2Finternational%2Farticles-reports%2F2021%2F12%2F13%2Fwhat-do-europeans-and-americans-think-about-nuclea).

Wind turbines, solar panels and related components are also being produced at increasing scale. [Surging solar manufacturing capacity](https://ember-climate.org/insights/research/china-solar-exports/) is expected to reach nearly 1,000 gigawatts annually in 2024 – double what was produced in 2022.

### Wind and solar are among the cleanest power sources
Once installed, virtually no greenhouse gases are emitted as a result of wind and solar power generation, and they pay off the energy related to their manufacturing and construction within a matter of [months](https://www.vestas.com/en/sustainability/environment/energy-payback). Their existence prevents the continuous burning of fossil fuels for decades.

Over the course of a typical 3 megawatt wind turbine’s 25 year lifespan, [154,484 tonnes of coal would need to be burned](https://www.distilled.earth/p/this-anti-renewable-energy-meme-is) to produce the equivalent amount of power. This would emit around 400,000 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere – roughly the same as driving an average petrol car around the equator [50,000 times](https://ourworldindata.org/travel-carbon-footprint).

Global [power sector emissions would have been 20% higher](https://ember-climate.org/insights/research/global-electricity-review-2023/#chapter-3-the-big-picture-a-new-era-of-declining-power-sector-emissions) in 2022 if all the electricity from wind and solar had instead come from fossil generation.
